survivingClaim: MEASURED: for 500- and 2000-zero windows at heights 1e3 to 1e8 (plus referee blocks at 3e5, 3e7) and P = 10 to 1e5, A_S at zeta zeros over N_w*M_P is below 1 and equals 1 - 2c_P/L (c_P = sum_{p<=P} log p/(p-1), L = log(T/2pi); classical Landau-Gonek first-order term) within 0.014 for c_P/L below about 0.28, and is about 0.022 x^-2.87 for x >= 0.6 (fit, heuristic exponent). The bound is not uniform in height at fixed P and not uniform in window length (fails for 25-zero windows), and fails against the one-spacing shifted reference (max 1.17). The Davenport-Heilbronn formal partial product at DH zeros (on-line and off-line; reproduced independently, also against the continuous t-mean) and the Liouville twist at rho/2 (in the mean) show the same one-sided suppression, so the quantity does not discriminate zeta from controls. Lead closed; no statement about zero locations.

lesson: Suppression of a truncated Dirichlet series at its own zeros is the Landau-Gonek diagonal term. It needs only the prime-power coefficients of -F'/F, holds for DH at on-line and off-line zeros, and depends on log P / log T, so it cannot discriminate zero location. Shifts within one mean spacing are not an independent reference (they tend to half the mean); use the continuous t-mean.
